page.title: Microsoft Entra ID
page.subtitle: Federate McHarbor login to an Azure AD tenant. Plugin handles the OIDC authorization-code flow against the v2.0 endpoints at login.microsoftonline.com plus the Microsoft Graph API for admin-group fetch.
page.registerHint: Add a provider from the host's Settings > Security > Identity Providers page and pick "Microsoft Entra ID" as the provider_type.

help.tenant_id: Azure AD tenant ID (UUID). Use 'common' for multi-tenant apps, 'organizations' for any work or school account, or leave 'common' for personal accounts too.
help.client_id: Application (client) ID from the App Registration overview page.
help.client_secret: Client secret value from the App Registration's Certificates & secrets page. Stored encrypted at rest.
help.scopes: Space-separated OAuth scopes. Defaults to openid profile email. Use 'https://graph.microsoft.com/.default' to enable group fetching via the Graph API.

guide.title: Set up Microsoft Entra ID in McHarbor
guide.subtitle: Register a confidential client application in your Azure AD tenant and grant Microsoft Graph permissions if you want admin-group fetching enabled.

step1.title: Open the App Registration blade
step1.body: In the Azure portal, navigate to Microsoft Entra ID > App registrations > New registration. Pick a name (e.g. "McHarbor SSO") and select the account types you want to support (single-tenant, multi-tenant, or personal).

step2.title: Set the redirect URI
step2.body: Under Redirect URI, pick Web and enter the McHarbor callback URL shown on the provider edit page. The host appends /api/identity-providers/callback to your McHarbor base URL — copy it exactly to avoid silent auth-code mismatches.

step3.title: Create a client secret
step3.body: Open Certificates & secrets > New client secret. Pick a sensible expiry (90 or 180 days) and set a calendar reminder. Copy the secret VALUE (not the Secret ID) into the Client Secret field on the provider form. McHarbor stores it AES-256-GCM encrypted.

step4.title: Copy the Application (client) ID
step4.body: Back on the App Registration overview page, copy the Application (client) ID into the Client ID field on the provider form.

step5.title: Copy the Directory (tenant) ID
step5.body: Still on the overview page, copy the Directory (tenant) ID into the Tenant ID field on the provider form. Use "common" if you registered the app as multi-tenant.

step6.title: (Optional) Grant Microsoft Graph Group.Read.All
step6.body: If you want the admin group's group-mapping wizard to populate Entra groups, open API permissions > Add a permission > Microsoft Graph > Application permissions > Group.Read.All. Click Grant admin consent for <tenant>.

step7.title: Test the connection
step7.body: Back in McHarbor, click "Test connection" on the provider form. A green result means the OIDC discovery document resolved and a client-credentials token exchange succeeded against login.microsoftonline.com — the configuration is valid. You can now enable the provider and use "Sign in with Microsoft" on the login page.
